subject: spanish
title: Stamp 2: Foreign Intervention and Guernica
welcome_lead: Stamp the international dimension of the war and the bombing of Guernica.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on International Brigades, German and Italian intervention, and Guernica 1937.

concepts.def: International Brigades; foreign volunteers who fought for the Republic from 1936.
German air unit sent by Hitler to support Franco.
Italian expeditionary force sent by Mussolini.
Bombing of Guernica on 26 April 1937 by Legion Condor and Italian aircraft.
Picasso's 1937 painting denouncing the bombing; now in Museo Reina Sofia, Madrid.
Non-Intervention Committee; ineffective international body led by Britain and France.

walkthroughs.body_html: The International Brigades brought around 35,000 volunteers from over 50 countries to fight fascism. Famous units included the Lincoln Battalion (USA) and the British Battalion.
On 26 April 1937, market day in Guernica, the Basque town was bombed for hours by Nazi and Italian aircraft. The atrocity inspired Picasso's giant mural, displayed at the 1937 Paris World Fair.

While Britain and France enforced an arms embargo on the Republic, Germany and Italy openly supported Franco. The Soviet Union supplied the Republic, with Mexican backing. This imbalance proved decisive.
